content: The Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) is a comprehensive, prospective, multinational observational study that focuses on patients hospitalized with acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The primary objective of GRACE is to enhance the quality of care for ACS patients by analyzing variations in patient characteristics, treatment practices, and both in-hospital and post-discharge outcomes across hospitals worldwide. The study involves 73 hospitals equipped with on-site angiographic facilities across 14 countries, including North America, South America, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. A total of 24,189 patients were enrolled in the study. The participating hospitals were selected based on local demographic characteristics and available hospital resources to ensure a representative sample of ACS patients from each country. Patients were identified using either active or passive surveillance methods. For all enrolled patients, a standardized core case report form was completed. This form collected detailed information on patient demographics, medical history, acute symptoms, clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic findings, treatment strategies, and in-hospital outcomes. Additionally, patients were followed up six months after hospital discharge to document recurrent coronary events, medication usage, and mortality. The data collected through the GRACE project provides critical and extensive insights into the demographic and clinical profiles of ACS patients, current treatment practices, and patient outcomes across multiple countries. In the context of evidence-based medicine, the findings from GRACE offer a valuable multinational perspective on these outcomes. Furthermore, the study identifies variations in clinical practice, which can inform new strategies to improve patient care and optimize treatment approaches globally.
